subtype: Approach: noticing when grief becomes overwhelming and seeking support [Revision]
passage: Counsellor's note, Asif. Akash came in with his mother on Monday. His father died in March, and for weeks he seemed to be coping. Now, he said, he reads the same line four times, lies awake into the small hours, and feels ashamed of it. On Sunday he finally told his mother, who phoned the school that morning. I listened, and told him that asking for help months later is a sensible step, not a weakness. His mother stayed and held his hand. We agreed to meet weekly, and I will tell his teachers only what he allows. Since the sleep trouble has gone on for a while, I also suggested his mother check with the family doctor if it keeps going or worries them.

qa.q: How does Akash feel about his difficulty?
qa.a: Akash feels ashamed and worn out, since he reads the same line four times and lies awake into the small hours.

qa.q: What could Akash do besides the weekly meetings?
qa.a: Akash could keep telling his mother and the counsellor how he is, and if the sleep trouble goes on, check with the doctor.

qa.q: How might Akash's mother feel about his telling her?
qa.a: Akash's mother is probably worried but relieved he told her, since she phoned the school that morning and stayed to hold his hand.

grounding: Months later a student still cannot concentrate or sleep, tells his mother, who arranges a talk with a school counsellor, an appropriate step and not a weakness.

subtype: Approach: noticing when grief becomes overwhelming and seeking support [Revision]
passage:
Tuesday, 11 pm
Five months since Appachan died, and I still read the same page of chemistry four times. I lie awake till two, then sleep through the alarm. Ujjwal asked today why I don't come for football any more. I said I'm tired. That's true, but it's not the whole thing.
I kept thinking it would pass. Everyone said the first months are hard. But it isn't getting lighter. It's getting heavier.
So tonight, when Amma was sitting with her tea, I told her. Not everything, but enough: the not sleeping, the chemistry, how I feel like I'm underwater. She put her cup down and held my hand. She said it isn't weakness, it's a lot of grief, and that tomorrow she'll call Mrs. Thomas, the school counsellor, to set up a talk. Then she stayed up with me till I felt sleepy.
Jomon

qa.q: How long ago did Appachan die?
What made Jomon decide to tell Amma?
qa.a: Jomon felt the grief getting heavier instead of lighter and was worn out from not sleeping or concentrating.

qa.q: What else could help Jomon alongside the counsellor?
qa.a: Jomon could tell Ujjwal a little of what's happening and go back to football slowly, so friends and routine are part of the support too.

qa.q: How does Amma see Jomon's struggle?
qa.a: Amma sees it as a lot of grief rather than weakness, and responds that night by holding Jomon's hand and planning to call the counsellor.

grounding: Shows a student who still cannot sleep or concentrate months after a death telling the mother, who arranges a talk with the school counsellor.

passage:
Pradeep: you missed the test again
Madhav: couldn't get up. slept at 4
Pradeep: that's like every night now
Madhav: since Bhaiya died. it's been four months and I can't read one page without drifting off
Pradeep: have you told your mom
Madhav: she's sad enough already. I don't want to add to it
Pradeep: she'd want to know. this isn't laziness, it's grief
Madhav: maybe
Pradeep: tonight? I'll stay online
(10:50 pm)
Madhav: told Mummy
Pradeep: and??
Madhav: she cried a bit. then said she's been worried about me too
Madhav: she's calling the school counsellor tomorrow morning and she's coming with me
Madhav: we're sitting in the kitchen with tea right now. I feel lighter
Pradeep: proud of you

qa.q: What time did Madhav fall asleep the night before the test?
Why was Madhav holding back from telling Mummy?
qa.a: Madhav felt protective and worried about adding to Mummy's sadness, since she was already grieving Bhaiya.

qa.q: What else could help Madhav alongside the counsellor?
qa.a: Madhav could tell a class teacher about the missed tests, so the school can ease the load while things are hard.

qa.q: How does Mummy respond to what Madhav tells her?
qa.a: Mummy is upset but glad to know, saying she had been worried too, and acts at once by planning to go with Madhav to the counsellor.

grounding: Illustrates a student noticing months later that grief is stopping sleep and study, telling the mother, and getting a counsellor meeting arranged.
